newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Belarus start last-minute talks on treaty.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Belarus start last-minute talks on treaty.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, due to sign a Union Treaty with his Belarussian counterpart Alexander Lukashenko on Wednesday, met Lukashenko at 9 a.m. (0500 GMT) for last minute talks, a Kremlin spokesman said.

The document aims to tighten ties between the two former Soviet republics, but Yeltsin's aides and ministers have been wrangling about exactly what form the agreement should take. Lukashenko had flown to Moscow earlier than scheduled but had originally only been due to meet Yeltsin at 11 a.m.

The signing of the treaty has been scheduled for noon (0800 GMT) but the text of the document has not been made public, clearly because of last-minute wrangling between liberals and conservatives in the Russian administration.

A draft of the "Treaty on a Union of Belarus and Russia", obtained by Reuters on Monday, provided for the two former Soviet republics to coordinate foreign, economic and defence policies, but stopped short of a merger into a single state.
Yeltsin publicly backed the treaty on Tuesday and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin insisted it would be signed.

But Russian liberals have launched a rearguard action against the draft. They fear the union could harm Russia's economy and make Lukashenko, who once professed an admiration for Adolf Hitler, a key player in Moscow politics.
